findings.title: HTTP handling waits for the client to close the connection
findings.description: read_to_end waits for EOF instead of stopping after the request headers and Content-Length bytes. Normal HTTP/1.1 clients keep the connection open while awaiting the response, so requests hang indefinitely.

findings.title: Missing or malformed Authorization headers panic
findings.description: bearer_token indexes parts[1] unconditionally. Server::handle calls it even when the header is absent, so an ordinary unauthenticated request panics its handler instead of receiving a 401 response.

findings.title: The running server has no way to create a valid session
findings.description: The server initializes an Authenticator with an empty private session map, but no startup path or endpoint calls issue. Consequently every syntactically valid bearer token is rejected and none of the service endpoints can be used.

findings.title: Creating a link for any new owner panics
findings.description: The quota map starts empty and create calls get_mut(owner).unwrap(). There is no path that initializes an owner's quota entry, so the first valid link creation panics.

findings.title: Link expiration logic is inverted
findings.description: A link is marked expired when now is earlier than expires_at. Fresh links are therefore removed on their first resolution, while already-expired links remain resolvable until another cleanup path removes them.

findings.title: Partial final pages panic with an out-of-bounds slice
findings.description: When offset + size exceeds the number of links, end is set to all.len() + 1. The subsequent slice is always out of bounds. The default page size therefore panics whenever a nonempty store contains fewer than 20 links.

findings.title: Stats endpoint divides by zero for an empty store
findings.description: hits is divided by guard.len() without handling zero links. Requesting stats on a fresh or fully-pruned store panics the handler.

findings.title: Configuration validation always accepts invalid settings
findings.description: validate collects and logs invalid port and timeout errors but unconditionally returns Ok. Startup therefore proceeds with configurations that the method explicitly identifies as unusable.

findings.title: Cache TTL milliseconds are interpreted as seconds
findings.description: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is documented as milliseconds, but its parsed value is passed to Duration::from_secs. For example, 5000 configures roughly 83 minutes instead of five seconds.

findings.title: Cache utilization is miscalculated and can panic
findings.description: Integer division happens before multiplication, so utilization reports 0% for every non-full cache. If LINKD_CACHE_SIZE is zero, this expression divides by zero.

findings.title: Invalid or overflowing TTL input is silently accepted
findings.description: A malformed ttl becomes zero, while multiplying an arbitrary u64 by 3600 can panic in checked builds or wrap in optimized builds. The endpoint can return 201 with an unintended expiry or terminate the handler.

findings.title: A report with the default name is written and then read under different names
findings.description: export_csv maps an empty name to links.csv, but read_report receives the original empty name and attempts to read .csv. GET /report without a name therefore writes a report and then returns a 500 error.

findings.title: Snapshot installation failures are reported as success
findings.description: The result of rename is discarded. A missing destination directory, permission failure, or cross-filesystem rename leaves no snapshot.json, yet write_snapshot returns Ok.

findings.title: Archive writes silently ignore I/O failures
findings.description: Each write result is discarded, so disk-full and other write failures can produce truncated owner archives while archive_all returns Ok.

findings.title: Rename validates the source code twice instead of validating the destination
findings.description: The second validate_code call also receives from. Invalid destination codes can consequently be inserted into the store.

findings.title: Success rate truncates before converting to a percentage
findings.description: used / self.links.len() is integer division, so the result is 0 unless every link has been used. For example, one used link out of two is reported as 0% instead of 50%.

findings.title: Deleting links never returns their quota slots
findings.description: delete removes the link but does not decrement its owner's quota count. Quota data becomes permanently inflated after deletions, contrary to the method's contract.

findings.title: Top links are returned in ascending hit order
findings.description: The comparator sorts least hits first and truncate retains those entries, so top(n) returns the least-followed links rather than the most-followed links.

findings.title: Owner lookup matches substrings instead of exact owners
findings.description: by_owner uses contains, so querying owner ann also returns links owned by joann or anna. The returned collection does not satisfy the documented exact-owner filter.

findings.title: Extending a link revives already-expired links
findings.description: extend unconditionally replaces expires_at with a future time. This contradicts the stated final-expiry behavior and makes dead codes live again.

findings.title: Batch import is not atomic
findings.description: Links are validated and inserted one at a time. If a later link has an invalid code, earlier links remain stored even though import returns Err, violating the all-or-nothing contract.

findings.title: Prune returns the number of links remaining instead of removed
findings.description: The pre-prune count is discarded and the method returns self.links.len(). Callers receive the opposite quantity from the documented removal count.

findings.title: Admin-role check rejects every possible role
findings.description: A role cannot simultaneously equal both admin and owner, so the OR condition is always true and require_admin always returns an error, including for administrators.

findings.title: Expired sessions continue to verify successfully
findings.description: verify only compares token strings and never checks expires_at. Tokens remain accepted indefinitely despite their configured 12-hour lifetime.

findings.title: Cache eviction is arbitrary rather than least-recently-used
findings.description: set removes the first hash-map key and never consults Entry.used. When capacity is reached, recently accessed entries can be evicted while older entries remain.

findings.title: Persistent connections consume unbounded handler threads
findings.description: Each accepted connection gets a new OS thread which calls read_to_end without a deadline. A normal HTTP/1.1 client waits for the response while keeping its connection open, so the server waits for EOF and the client waits for the server. Slow or malicious clients can therefore accumulate permanently blocked threads until the process exhausts resources.

findings.title: Handlers retain the global store mutex during blocking I/O
findings.description: Named MutexGuards remain alive through calls to respond in create_link and several other handlers; report additionally keeps the guard during filesystem work. If one client stops reading its response or an export blocks, that handler retains the only store lock while every other store-dependent handler waits, causing service-wide contention and allowing a slow client to stall the service.

findings.title: Concurrent resolved-counter increments are lost
findings.description: add_resolved implements an increment as a separate atomic load and store. Two handler threads can both load N and both store N+1, losing one resolved event and making the dashboard undercount traffic.

findings.title: Cache get and flush acquire locks in opposite orders
findings.description: get holds entries and then locks hits, while flush holds hits and then locks entries. If get acquires entries as flush acquires hits, each thread waits for the lock held by the other and both deadlock.

findings.title: Cache sweep can delete a concurrently refreshed entry
findings.description: sweep identifies expired codes under a read lock, releases that lock, and deletes each code later. Between those operations another thread can set the same code with a fresh expiration; sweep then deletes the new entry based on the obsolete observation.

findings.title: Janitor stop can return before another sweep and dropping it never stops the thread
findings.description: The worker checks the channel before sleeping, while stop only sends and never joins. If stop is called just after the check, it returns immediately but the janitor sleeps for the full interval and performs another mutation before observing the signal. Dropping JanitorStop disconnects the channel, but try_recv errors are ignored, so the detached thread then runs forever while retaining the store and cache Arcs.

findings.title: warm_cache returns before its worker threads finish
findings.description: The spawned JoinHandles are discarded rather than joined, contradicting the function's completion guarantee. A caller can invoke warm_cache and immediately read the cache before any spawned setter runs, observing a miss even though warming supposedly completed.

findings.title: count_by_owner deadlocks by relocking the same mutex
findings.description: The first MutexGuard remains alive when the function calls store.lock() again. Rust's standard Mutex is not reentrant, so any call to count_by_owner blocks forever on its own lock.

findings.title: Concurrent snapshots race through one shared temporary file
findings.description: Every write_snapshot call uses /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json. Two concurrent snapshots can truncate and write the same inode, interleave content, or have one call rename the file while the other is still using it. The losing rename error is ignored, so both calls may report success even though snapshot.json contains the wrong or corrupted payload.

findings.title: Unauthenticated clients can exhaust server resources
findings.description: Each accepted connection receives a new OS thread, and that thread calls read_to_end without a timeout or size limit before authentication. A remote attacker can hold many connections open indefinitely or send unbounded bodies, exhausting threads, file descriptors, or memory and denying service.

findings.title: Session tokens are predictable from their issuance time
findings.description: Token generation seeds a deterministic LCG with the current time in whole seconds and does not incorporate the configured secret. An attacker who knows approximately when a session was issued can reproduce the few candidate tokens and impersonate that session; sessions issued in the same second also receive the same token.

findings.title: Expired access tokens remain valid indefinitely
findings.description: verify returns a matching session without comparing expires_at to the current time. Consequently, a stolen token continues authorizing requests after its advertised 12-hour lifetime and remains useful until explicitly revoked.

findings.title: Authenticated identity is discarded, eliminating tenant isolation
findings.description: The server verifies a token but discards its Session and dispatches handlers without the authenticated owner. A holder of any valid token can supply another owner on creation, obtain every tenant's links through /report, and delete any known code because those handlers cannot enforce ownership.

findings.title: Stored link targets allow HTTP response splitting
findings.description: A target is accepted when it merely starts with http:// or https://, so a POST body can store a target containing CRLF characters. When that link is resolved, redirect_to writes the value directly into the Location header, allowing the creator to inject arbitrary response headers or an additional response into requests made by other users of the link.

findings.title: Report names permit writes outside the export directory
findings.description: The authenticated name query parameter is joined directly to the export directory. Values containing ../ escape that directory, while an absolute name causes Path::join to discard the configured directory entirely. The subsequent fs::write truncates or creates the selected .csv path with service privileges, enabling unauthorized file overwrite and disk-filling attacks.

findings.title: Client-controlled header grants administrator access
findings.description: The administrator endpoint authorizes requests solely when the caller supplies X-Admin: true; it never checks the verified session's role. Any authenticated user can therefore invoke the administrator-only endpoint and retrieve tenant quota information.

findings.title: Unescaped owner values enable CSV formula injection
findings.description: User-controlled owner values are inserted into CSV cells without quoting or formula neutralization. An attacker can choose an owner beginning with =, +, -, or @ so that support personnel opening the generated report in spreadsheet software execute an attacker-controlled formula, potentially causing data exfiltration or malicious external requests.

findings.title: Live access tokens are written to application logs
findings.description: Every issued bearer token is printed in full. Anyone with access to console output, centralized logs, or retained diagnostics can copy the token and impersonate its owner, and the missing expiry enforcement makes that access persist until revocation.

findings.title: Malformed Authorization headers remotely panic request handlers
findings.description: bearer_token indexes parts[1] without checking that it exists. Every request without an Authorization header, or with a one-part malformed value, panics its spawned handler thread; an unauthenticated attacker can generate these panics rapidly to consume CPU and fill panic logs.
